title: Campaign
description: A grouping of content, product references, and timing for a coordinated marketing push for Rough Draft Builders Club (RDBC). This is a schema *contract* only (architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §8); no runtime enforces it yet (src/ does not exist before Phase 16). `product_ids`/`content_ids` are plain `format: uuid` reference fields with no runtime referential-integrity enforcement — no adapter or database exists yet to check that a referenced id actually resolves to a real product or content record (architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §7, no writer role is granted for real entity records today). `approval_id` links this record to a campaign-level approval, distinct from and in addition to any approval each individual linked content item carries on its own `content.schema.json` record — see this schema's `approval_id` property description for the reasoning. See architecture/STATE_MACHINE.md for this entity's documented lifecycle transitions between `status` values.

id.description: Server-assigned identity. Never client-supplied, never reused. Shared envelope field, architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1.

schema_version.description: The exact semver version of campaign.schema.json this record was written against. architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1, §3.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-chosen deduplication key; a create request whose idempotency_key matches an existing campaign record returns the existing record rather than creating a duplicate. architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1, §4.

status.description: This campaign's own lifecycle status — distinct from the linked approval record's status (`approval_id` below; architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §6). Enum values and reasoning are this schema's own design choice (Data Architect, Phase 04); transitions between them are documented separately in architecture/STATE_MACHINE.md, which cites this exact enum. DRAFT: the campaign concept and its grouping of content/products/timing are being assembled and have not been finalized. PLANNED: the campaign's scope is finalized and, where applicable, its approval has been requested or granted, but its planned start has not yet arrived. ACTIVE: the campaign is currently running. PAUSED: the campaign was active and has been temporarily halted without being completed — distinct from ARCHIVED, which is a terminal retirement. COMPLETED: the campaign ran its planned course and concluded normally. ARCHIVED: the campaign is retired from active consideration, whether it completed, was paused indefinitely, or never left DRAFT/PLANNED.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339. Set once, never mutated. architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339. Set on every accepted mutation; must be >= created_at. architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1.

created_by_role.description: Which role created this record — a closed role token from policy/action_registry.json's `roles` array, never a person's name or an invented role. architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1.

name.description: A short structural label for this campaign — no example value here resembles a real RDBC campaign name (architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §1's data-minimisation rule, extended project-wide).

description.description: A structural description of what this campaign is intended to accomplish. Any external-facing statement this text implies (a claim, a discount, a controversial-topic position) is itself subject to the corresponding gated category (CLAUDE.md §4) before publication, independent of this campaign record existing.

approval_id.description: References the approval record (APPROVAL_POLICY.md §2; schemas/approval.schema.json) governing this campaign as a whole, if any request has been submitted. Null until a campaign-level approval request exists. Campaign-level approval is a deliberate design choice, kept separate from each linked content item's own `approval_id` on `content.schema.json`: a campaign can itself constitute a coordinated action requiring sign-off distinct from any single piece of content within it — for example, a campaign that bundles a discount (GC-03) or commits to a timed public push touching a controversial topic (GC-07) is a decision at the campaign level, not fully captured by approving its individual content pieces one at a time. This field does not substitute for, and is not substituted by, any individual content item's own approval_id.

product_ids.description: The products this campaign concerns, referenced by id. Plain reference list with no runtime referential-integrity enforcement (architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §7) — nothing checks that a listed id resolves to a real product.schema.json record. May be an empty array, e.g. while the campaign is still in DRAFT and its product scope is not yet decided.

content_ids.description: The content items grouped under this campaign, referenced by id. Plain reference list with no runtime referential-integrity enforcement (architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §7) — nothing checks that a listed id resolves to a real content.schema.json record. May be an empty array, e.g. while the campaign is still in DRAFT and no content has been drafted for it yet.

planned_start_at.description: The campaign's intended start date-time, ISO 8601 / RFC 3339. Null until a start has been planned. Structural only — this schema imposes no minimum lead time, staleness window, or other numeric business rule around this value (D-047: no numeric threshold is invented).

planned_end_at.description: The campaign's intended end date-time, ISO 8601 / RFC 3339. Null until an end has been planned, or for a campaign with no defined end. Structural only — this schema imposes no minimum/maximum duration or other numeric business rule around this value (D-047: no numeric threshold is invented).
